title: Kenyan Sweet Mandazi
author: Mama Wanjiru

relatedDish.note: Sweet Mandazi (KEN105) uses more sugar than classic Mandazi (KEN015) and is often dusted with icing sugar after frying — making it more of a dessert treat than a breakfast accompaniment. Classic mandazi (KEN015) is the everyday version; sweet mandazi is the indulgent, treat version.

desc: Kenyan Sweet Mandazi — a sweeter, more indulgent version of the beloved fried bread, dusted with icing sugar and fragrant with vanilla and cardamom. Closer to a doughnut in sweetness — a treat version of the Kenyan everyday classic.
longDesc: Sweet mandazi pushes the classic in the direction of a treat — more sugar in the dough, a touch of vanilla, and a generous dusting of icing sugar after frying that makes it feel celebratory and indulgent. Children particularly love this version, and it is a popular choice for school parties, celebrations, and any occasion where mandazi is called for but something a little more special is wanted.
ingredients: ¾ cup sugar — more than classic mandazi
1 cup coconut milk or whole milk
steps: Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Mix milk, warm water, egg, melted butter, and vanilla.
Combine wet and dry ingredients into a soft dough.
Roll to 1cm thick. Cut into triangles or squares.
Fry at 170°C for 2—3 minutes per side until deep golden.
Dust generously with icing sugar while still warm. Serve immediately.
chefTips: Dust with icing sugar while the mandazi is still warm — it melts slightly and adheres better.
The extra sugar means they brown more quickly — watch the oil temperature carefully.
A pinch of cinnamon mixed with the icing sugar adds another layer of warmth.
commonMistakes: Too high oil temperature — the extra sugar burns the outside.
Too much icing sugar — becomes cloyingly sweet.
storage: Best eaten the day they are made. Store in airtight container for up to 2 days.
reheating: Warm in oven at 160°C for 5 minutes. Re-dust with icing sugar before serving.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as an occasional treat rather than an everyday food.
culturalNote: Sweet mandazi is the treat version of Kenya's favourite fried bread — prepared for children's celebrations, school parties, and any occasion that calls for something a little more indulgent than the everyday classic.
